newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - PHILIPPINE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - PHILIPPINE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 14.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Senate President Ernesto Maceda says the Senate will oppose any move to convene the Congress into a Constituent Assembly to change the constitution. (MANILA BULLETIN/MALAYA/CHRONICLE)

- The Senate will move to strip Presidential Security Adviser Jose Almonte of his power to supervise and control over the government's spying apparatus, Senate President Pro Tempore Blas Ople says. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- President Fidel Ramos is set to meet 16 of the 24 senators to thresh out their differences. (MANILA TIMES)

- Socialite Rosemarie Arenas denies she is lobbying for the reversal of the Supreme Court decision on the People's Initiative for Reform, Modernisation and Action, challenging her accuser Senator Miriam Defensor-Santiago to prove her claim. (MANILA CHRONICLE)
- The central bank cut its overnight borrowing rate to 14 percent from 18 percent to further bring domestic interest rates down to normal level. (ALL PAPERS)

- The Securities and Exchange Commission is set to impose a combined penalty of 950,000 pesos on four brokerage firms accused by columnist Ninez Cacho-Olivares of mishandling her investment account. (MANILA TIMES)
- The Unitd States has renewed its Generalised System of Preferences scheme until June 30 next year which will benefit about 20 percent of Philippine exports to the United States. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
